title: Lenovo - Legion Pro 27Q-10 Longterm review (short); incredible MOTION RESOLUTION "for the win".

comments.text: How is the hdr performance of this monitor I was thinking of buying this as my first oled monitor
comments.author: @satyamwathrey7704

comments.text:
Like anything HDR..
Source matters!


Streaming HDR is very poor.
4K UHDs are fantastic.
HDR consoles (eg PS5 and Switch 2) are going to provide 'mixed' results.


If an HDR system is well setup (to match the source output).. generally good results..

But;
Depends on time of day viewing habits.

Eg I bought a 2025 Samsung 'the frame' TV, not OLED, and by the spec sheet "vastly worse" for HDR etc..

Except:
That 65"TV has a much larger screen area.
Even if it's peak brightness isn't HDR small monitor equivalent, it is actually much much brighter simply due to screen size.

Size matters.

HDR if your source handles HDR easily (eg not Windows PCs!)..
Is alright..
But SDR and normal brightness range matters!

This Lenovo monitor has issues due to the IT spoofs 4K receive capable..
This has caught me out many times.

So I moved (temporary) to the TV.
TV takes 3800x1600 Ultrawide signal, no fear of breaking (bright screen static or black bars borders for lengthy time periods), and massively outpunches the HDR capability of this small OLED.

Except for black values.

A lamp behind screen nullifies this benefit.. (eyes adjust and reset black point)

comments.text: Great point. I bought it and it is on the way. For me motion clarity is very important especially because I play valorant somewhat competitively. I will see how it performs for me...
comments.author: @userben6791

comments.text:
motion rate; being a spec that consumers generally are NOT AWARE to be checking (assuming they get motion res equal to panel res), has been in decline for decades.
CRT=full motion res.
early digital panels spent a lot to achieve decent motion res, and when the price wars started to seriously lower 'flat panel' prices colour bit depth (6bit/6bit and frc etc) and motion resolution going super low were casualties.

My partner had a 720p TV that had more motion res than most 4K panels being sold.
As does this monitor; very very few 4K panels (TV especially) will touch this level of motion resolution.

It is a genuine 10bit colour panel as well.

Colour and contrast matter MOST, but having pixels that update fast enough (all colours equally quick!) is paramount for some content types.

Hope you enjoy your top tier panel.
I was amazed it handshook with proper 4K, spoofing the consoles that it WAS a 4K screen.
Awesome!!
